description: VSEL Reordered Trace - Attack: Trace Reordering
attack_vector: Swap order of dependent transfers to hide insufficient balance error

correct_execution_order.expected_result: FAILURE - insufficient balance (USER_B only has 800 from first transfer + 500 original - any sent = ~1300, but then after A->B 800, B has 1300, then B sends 900 to C = 400 remaining. Actually let me reconsider...)
correct_execution_order._corrected_expected_result: SUCCESS - USER_B received 800 from USER_A plus original 500 = 1300, can send 900 to USER_C

_attack_mechanism.description: By reordering entries, we make it appear that transfer B->C happened when USER_B had sufficient balance from original 500, but in reality transfer A->B must happen first to make B->C valid. If A->B is processed first, A has insufficient funds (1000-800=200) and subsequent transfers from A would fail.
_attack_mechanism.causal_dependency: Transfer B->C depends on B receiving from A first
_attack_mechanism.why_reordering_hides_issue: In reordered trace, B->C appears to execute when B has only 500, which would actually fail if executed in that order
_attack_mechanism.actual_vulnerability: Reordering makes invalid execution appear valid, or valid execution appear in invalid order

input._note: In actual execution, this would fail because USER_B only has 500

post_state._invalid_state: USER_B has negative balance - this state is impossible
post_state._how_attack_works: Trace shows this as valid, but in reality this transition would violate non-negative balance invariant

metadata._reordering_indicator: This entry claims to be index 0 but depends on state from entry that should be first

post_state._inconsistent: Pre-state assumes B already sent 900, but B couldn't have sent 900 without receiving from A first

_causal_inconsistency.description: The trace claims execution order [B->C, A->B] but B cannot send 900 before receiving from A
_causal_inconsistency.pre_state_mismatch: Entry 1 claims pre-state where B has already sent 900, but B only had 500 initially
_causal_inconsistency.balance_violation: Entry 0 shows B with -400 balance, violating non-negative balance invariant
_causal_inconsistency.detection_requirement: Verifier must check that pre-state of each entry is reachable from post-state of previous entries

_attack_explanation.how_it_works: The trace entries are swapped. The post-state of entry 0 (B sends 900) is impossible because B only had 500. However, the trace shows a valid-looking commitment chain.
_attack_explanation.detection_strategy: Verify causal dependencies: B's transfer requires sufficient balance which only exists after receiving from A. Check that pre_state_commitment of entry N matches post_state_commitment of entry N-1.
_attack_explanation.what_verifier_should_detect: State commitment discontinuity and causal violation - entry 0 creates impossible state

expected_verification._ordering_failure: Causal dependency violated - B cannot transfer 900 before receiving from A
expected_verification._semantic_binding_failure: Execution semantics don't match real-world causality
expected_verification._invariant_failure: Non-negative balance invariant violated in entry 0

expected_test_outcome.rejection_reason: Causal dependency violation - state commitment chain shows impossible transition
expected_test_outcome._specific_failure: Entry 0 requires balance that doesn't exist in initial state
expected_test_outcome._causal_analysis: Transfer from B to C requires B to have received from A first
